items.text: We reused the blind test we used for CL-SciSumm 2018 since we want to have a comparable evaluation CL-SciSumm 2019 systems that will have additional training data (see Section 3.1).
items.why: Identifies reusing a blind test set, creating potential dataset overlap or leakage.
items.plain: We reused the blind test set from the 2018 competition so we could compare performance with systems that had access to more training data.

items.text: Speciﬁcally, for Task 1, we used the method proposed by [17] to prepare noisy training data for about 1000 unannotated papers.
items.why: Mentions using an automated method to generate noisy training data.
items.plain: For Task 1, we used an automated matching method to create noisy training data for about 1,000 unannotated papers.

items.text: This is about 0.02 lower than the best CL-SciSumm’18 system [22] which was at 0.145.
items.why: Shows best score on Task 1a dropped compared to the previous year.
items.plain: The top F1 score for sentence overlap in Task 1a this year was 0.126, which is about 0.02 lower than the top score of 0.145 from 2018.

items.text: Traditional machine learning based systems such as [10] seem to suﬀer from noise in the augmented data.
items.why: Acknowledges that traditional machine learning models suffered from noisy augmented data.
items.plain: Traditional machine learning systems appear to perform worse because of noise in the automatically added training data.

items.text: In Task 1a the best performing CL-SciSumm ’19 system The best performing CL-SciSumm ’18 system [22] used traditional models including random forests and ranking models trained on the CL-SciSumm ’18 training data.
items.why: Claims traditional models on clean data beat deep learning on noisy data.
items.plain: In Task 1a, the best system from 2018 used traditional machine learning on clean data, showing that traditional models on clean data out-perform deep learning models on noisy data.

items.text: This implies that for Task 1a, traditional models trained on clean data perform better than deep learning models trained on noisy data.
items.why: Summarizes the comparative trade-off between model types and data noise.
items.plain: For Task 1a, traditional models trained on clean data outperform deep learning models trained on noisy data.

items.text: On Task 1b, systems using traditional methods perform better than deep learning systems.
items.why: Notes traditional methods outperformed deep learning models on Task 1b.
items.plain: For Task 1b, systems using traditional machine learning methods performed better than deep learning systems.

items.text: Deep learning methods take over on large bu tnoisy data.
items.why: States general claims on when deep learning vs traditional methods succeed.
items.plain: Traditional methods perform better on Task 1a when training data is small but clean, whereas deep learning methods perform better when given large but noisy data.
